questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle initiates the first 15 degrees of arm abduction at the glenohumeral joint?
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus muscle initiates abduction for the first 15 degrees before the deltoid takes over.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Injury to the axillary nerve most commonly impairs which of the following movements?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve innervates the deltoid muscle, which is responsible for arm abduction beyond 15 degrees.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following tendon structures is most frequently injured in rotator cuff tears?
questions.explanation: The supraspinatus tendon is the most commonly impinged and torn tendon in rotator cuff pathology.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Winged scapula resulting from long thoracic nerve injury is due to paralysis of which muscle?
questions.explanation: The long thoracic nerve innervates the serratus anterior muscle, which holds the scapula against the thoracic wall.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which nerve travels through the anatomical snuffbox and is at risk during scaphoid fractures?
questions.explanation: The superficial branch of the radial nerve crosses the anatomical snuffbox, along with the radial artery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus threatens which artery?
questions.explanation: The posterior circumflex humeral artery and axillary nerve run together around the surgical neck of the humerus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Mid-shaft humeral fractures are classically associated with damage to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The radial nerve runs in the radial groove along the mid-shaft of the humerus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nerves passes posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The ulnar nerve passes posterior to the medial epicondyle in the cubital tunnel.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient unable to flex the proximal interphalangeal joints of digits 1-3 likely has damage to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The median nerve innervates flexor digitorum superficialis, responsible for PIP joint flexion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Compression of the median nerve within the carpal tunnel spares cutaneous sensation over which region?
questions.explanation: The palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve arises proximal to the carpal tunnel and passes superficial to it.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which structure forms the lateral border of the anatomical snuffbox?
options: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
questions.explanation: The tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis form the anterior/lateral boundary of the anatomical snuffbox.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A fracture of the hook of the hamate typically injures which motor structure in the hand?
questions.explanation: The deep branch of the ulnar nerve passes adjacent to the hook of the hamate in Guyon's canal.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Loss of forearm flexion when the forearm is in a mid-pronated position indicates injury to which nerve?
questions.explanation: The brachioradialis flexes the forearm when semi-pronated and is innervated by the radial nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle is the principal medial rotator of the arm at the shoulder joint?
questions.explanation: Subscapularis inserts onto the lesser tubercle of the humerus and acts as the primary medial rotator.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: An Erb-Duchenne palsy ('waiter's tip' posture) results from damage to which brachial plexus roots?
questions.explanation: Erb-Duchenne palsy involves damage to the upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5-C6 roots).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Klumpke palsy causes a 'claw hand' deformity due to injury to which roots of the brachial plexus?
questions.explanation: Lower trunk brachial plexus injuries (C8-T1) cause Klumpke palsy, affecting intrinsic hand muscles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle adducts and medially rotates the humerus and is innervated by the thoracodorsal nerve?
questions.explanation: Latissimus dorsi extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm; it is innervated by the thoracodorsal nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which artery accompanies the radial nerve in the radial groove of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The profunda brachii artery travels alongside the radial nerve along the posterior shaft of the humerus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: At which point does the subclavian artery officially change its name to the axillary artery?
questions.explanation: The subclavian artery becomes the axillary artery at the lateral margin of the first rib.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which muscle forms the apex/floor of the cubital fossa laterally?
questions.explanation: The cubital fossa is bounded medially by pronator teres and laterally by brachioradialis.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Injury to the anterior interosseous nerve leads to inability to perform which action?
options: Make an 'OK' sign with thumb and index finger
questions.explanation: Anterior interosseous nerve innervates FPL and FDP to digit 2, essential for pinching/making an 'OK' sign.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Loss of sensation on the lateral aspect of the forearm indicates lesion of which cutaneous nerve?
questions.explanation: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve is the terminal sensory continuation of the musculocutaneous nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which carpal bone is most frequently dislocation anteriorly into the carpal tunnel?
questions.explanation: Dislocation of the lunate bone occurs anteriorly and can cause acute carpal tunnel compression.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which intrinsic hand muscle group is innervated by the recurrent branch of the median nerve?
questions.explanation: The recurrent branch of the median nerve innervates FPB, APB, and OP (thenar group).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which interosseous muscles are responsible for finger abduction away from the axial line?
questions.explanation: Dorsal interossei abduct the digits ('DAB'), whereas palmar interossei adduct ('PAD').

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: What is the primary action of the lumbrical muscles at the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints?
questions.explanation: Lumbricals flex MCP joints and extend proximal/distal interphalangeal joints.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus anteromedially threatens which major vascular structure?
questions.explanation: Anteromedial displacement in supracondylar humeral fractures can injure the brachial artery and median nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which cord of the brachial plexus gives rise to the musculocutaneous nerve?
questions.explanation: The musculocutaneous nerve arises directly from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which superficial vein drains the lateral side of the upper limb into the axillary vein?
questions.explanation: The cephalic vein travels on the lateral side of the arm and pierces the clavipectoral fascia to enter the axillary vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The tendon of which biceps head passes through the intertubercular groove of the humerus?
questions.explanation: The long head tendon of the biceps brachii passes through the intertubercular (bicipital) sulcus.
